title: Kimsuky used a fake VPN invoice ZIP to deliver HttpTroy backdoor - what detection/response rules would you add?
clean_text: Gen Digital reports a targeted spear-phish that dropped a 3-stage chain: small dropper → loader MemLoad (persistence via scheduled task AhnlabUpdate ) → backdoor HttpTroy which talks to load.auraria[.]org . The ZIP filename impersonated a VPN invoice: 250908_A_HK이노션_SecuwaySSL VPN Manager U100S 100user_견적서.zip. Capabilities include file transfer, screenshots, command exec, in-memory loads and strong obfuscation. Discussion prompts: What YARA / EDR heuristics would catch MemLoad / HttpTroy behaviours quickly? How would you tune mail gateway filtering to flag invoice-style ZIPs with SCR/EXE inside? Any good playbooks for triage when a scheduled task named like a vendor (e.g., AhnlabUpdate) appears? Be specific - share detections, IOCs (no raw malware), and playbook snippets. Follow for balanced coverage.
